author: reek
body: The parent labels itself, spawns a child, and strips the child's identity bit with process-restrict-cap before the child runs. The child then tries to read its own label and its parent's, and reports both over a kernel channel. Both reads must be refused.

author: reek
body: This is the gate, and until the readers were gated it did not exist. identity-whoami and identity-get-proc did range checks only, so restricting bit 15 changed nothing about them: this test applied a capability restriction and then asserted the restriction had no effect. It now asserts the denial. The positive direction -- an unrestricted child inherits the capability and reads successfully -- is held by identity-inherit and identity-get-proc-test.
